summary: RESOLVED before this research ran, and the blocker was mis-attributed. Task 292's Phase 5 deferred its deploy because `git status --short agent-system/` was non-empty, reported as sibling task 293's in-flight edits. 293 is now completed and committed (phases 1-8, HEAD aed07df8e), and the cycle-4 Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint already ran deploy-headless.sh, resyncing 7 extensions. All six of 292's target files (multi-task-creation-standard.md, commands/task.md, commands/errors.md, agents/meta-builder-agent.md, skills/skill-fix-it/SKILL.md, context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md) are byte-identical between the source store and the deployed .claude/ tree, and Component 0 'Task-Count Reasoning' is present in the deployed copies. Phase 5's deploy OBJECTIVE is therefore already satisfied; only its verification sub-steps remain unrun by 292 itself. Critically, `agent-system/` is STILL dirty right now (3 files), so the predicate that blocked Phase 5 is still false even with zero sibling work in flight -- the gate would block again on re-run.
root_cause: The gate's predicate is whole-tree cleanliness of agent-system/, but the actual hazard is narrower: that a whole-tree deploy would bundle ANOTHER WRITER'S semantically-incomplete work into .claude/. Whole-tree cleanliness is a bad proxy for that hazard, and in this repo it is permanently unsatisfiable, for two independent and verified reasons. (1) SELF-DEFEATING BY CONSTRUCTION: deploy-headless.sh's own first action (lines 294-315) is a pre-deploy line_count auto-repair that runs `--write` against the SOURCE agent-system/extensions/*/index-entries.json. Every deploy that corrects any line_count therefore dirties the very tree it demanded be clean. The current dirt in agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json is exactly this: pure line_count churn (status-markers.md 454->535, state-schema.json 427->440, state-management-schema.md 547->590, and batch-orchestration-guardrails.md 1651->1661, the last being 292's OWN Phase 5 edit). The precondition is thus non-idempotent: satisfying it is impossible immediately after any successful deploy. (2) PRE-EXISTING UNRELATED DIRT: agent-system/extensions/typst/index-entries.json and typst/scripts/typst-element-lint.sh were already modified at session start, last committed by unrelated long-past work, and intersect neither 292's nor 293's declared file_scope. Nothing in this batch can clean them, so the predicate was already false before 293 wrote a single byte -- meaning Phase 5 would have deferred even had the two tasks run strictly sequentially. The sibling-concurrency story in the handoff is a true-but-incidental observation, not the operative cause.
solution_path: Do not re-litigate deploy timing inside a plan phase; the orchestrator already owns it with a strictly better mechanism. The Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (~line 887) has NO tree-cleanliness predicate at all. It fires on either (a) this cycle's modified files touching orchestrator-critical paths or (b) a deploy_pending marker written by orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's completion-deploy gate, then deploys, verifies, and reconciles new verify-deploy findings against a pre-redeploy baseline, explicitly dismissing findings that are flaky or unrelated to the batch's own modified files (~line 1028). That is precisely the scope-aware judgment a binary `git status` test cannot make, and it is what actually unblocked this batch: it promoted 293 to completed post-deploy with no manual action. DURABLE RECOMMENDATIONS, in priority order. (i) Plan-authoring guidance should stop emitting whole-tree-cleanliness deploy preconditions in implementation phases; a phase that needs its edits deployed should declare that and let the checkpoint deploy, rather than shelling out to deploy-headless.sh behind a `git status` guard. (ii) If a phase-level guard is genuinely wanted, narrow the predicate from 'agent-system/ is clean' to 'the dirty set, MINUS deploy-generated index-entries.json line_count churn, intersects paths outside this task's declared file_scope' -- which is both satisfiable and actually aimed at the hazard. (iii) Worth recording that deploy-headless.sh writes to its own source store, since any future cleanliness check anywhere will hit the same non-idempotence. NEXT ACTION FOR 292: its remaining Phase 5 work is verification only, not deployment. The cycle-4 verify-deploy run already reported the relevant state -- gate 5 FAIL (3 manifest/cross-extension-override findings, pre-existing, owned by task 290) and gate 20 FAIL (eager-load total 68289 B over a 65950 B baseline, pre-existing, owned by task 289, with a NEW WARN that commands/orchestrate.md at 21328 B now exceeds its 21000 B ceiling as a direct consequence of 293's STAGE 0 restructure). None of these are 292's regressions, and Phase 5 should close by recording that attribution rather than by attempting a deploy that has already happened.
